$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT policy for a fresh installation.
The capability layer cannot start without this file, so it has to ship. The
builder's own copy is not the file to ship: it carries a live Google Cloud
project id belonging to a third party, a standing authorization naming an
internal mission, and a provider note recording a private decision. None of
that is true for, or any business of, someone who installs this product.
WHAT CHANGED FROM THE BUILDER'S COPY, AND NOTHING ELSE CHANGED:
* approvals.standingAuthorizations is empty. A standing authorization is a
pre-granted permission to perform one exact action with one exact set of
arguments without asking again. A fresh installation has granted none, so
an empty list is the truthful value -- and shipping the builder's would
have pre-authorized an API call against a project the installer does not
own and cannot reach.
* providers.discord is gone: Discord left the product on 2026-08-22 by owner
ruling, and the engine's policy no longer carries the namespace.
Everything else is the product's own default and is deliberately identical:
the approval action list, the research fetch bounds, the Tavily pool sizes
(which match the fallbacks in src/lib/providers/web.js) and the provider
enablement flags. `enabled` means the policy permits a provider, not that it
is usable -- every one of them still needs credentials the vault does not have
on a fresh machine.
limits.defaultDailySpendUsd is carried over unchanged at 100. It is a product
default rather than owner data, but a spending ceiling nobody chose is worth
a deliberate decision rather than inheritance; that decision belongs to the
payments work, not to packaging.
